(sec-module-robotics.models)=
# Module: robotics.models

This module contains robotics models; They can be imported by simply calling the functions,
which return the according robot dictionary;
the library is built on Denavit-Hartenberg Parameters and
Homogeneous Transformations (HT) to describe transformations and coordinate systems

- **Date**: 2021-01-10

(sec-models-manipulator3rsimple)=
## Function: Manipulator3RSimple

[`Manipulator3RSimple()`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/models.py#L46)

- **function description**: generate 3R manipulator as myRobot dictionary, settings are done in function
- **output**: myRobot dictionary
- **author**: Martin Sereinig
- **notes**: DH-parameters: [theta, d, a, alpha], according to P. Corke Values according to Wörnle simple example with l1=0 d=[h1 0 0]; theta=[beta1 beta2 beta3]; a=[l1 l2 l3]; alpha=[pi/2 0 0];


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`numericalInverseKinematicsTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/numericalInverseKinematicsTest.py) (TM)


(sec-models-manipulatorfrankaemikapanda)=
## Function: ManipulatorFrankaEmikaPanda

[`ManipulatorFrankaEmikaPanda(useDH = False, gripper = None)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/models.py#L140)

- **function description**: generate Franka Emika Panda manipulator as myRobot dictionary, settings are done in function
- **input**:
  - `useDH`: False: the joint frames and the parameters of the URDF, with simple collision shapes (#3373); True: the modified DH parameters of Gaz et al.
  - `gripper`: None: without the hand; 'hand': only with useDH=False, link 7 with the hand and its fingers (opening 0.04 each) and their collision shape
- **output**: myRobot dictionary
- **author**: Martin Sereinig
- **notes**: all Parameter according to Gaz et. al [GazDeLuca2019] DH-parameters(std): [theta, d, a, alpha], according to P. Corke masses, inertias and COM according to Gaz et al., w.r.t. the frames of the modified DH parameters (modDHKK, the dhMode of the dictionary); the last link frame is the flange, 0.107 after joint 7, in both conventions, so the COM of the last link is moved by -0.107 in z against Gaz et al.; the standard DH parameters give the same kinematics, but the inertia parameters are not transformed to their frames; both checked against the RTB's Panda (#3255)


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`serialRobotInverseKinematics.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/serialRobotInverseKinematics.py) (Ex), [`analyticInverseKinematicsTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/analyticInverseKinematicsTest.py) (TM)

(sec-models-manipulatorur5)=
## Function: ManipulatorUR5

[`ManipulatorUR5(useDH = False)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/models.py#L359)

- **function description**: generate UR5 manipulator as myRobot dictionary, settings are done in function
- **input**:
  - `useDH`: False: the joint frames, masses and limits of the URDF, with simple collision shapes; the centers of mass and inertias are those of the solids of its collision meshes, scaled to the masses of the links, as the inertias of the URDF are not physical for the wrist (#3373); True: the standard DH parameters of P. Corke
- **output**: myRobot dictionary
- **author**: Martin Sereinig
- **notes**: define myRobot kinematics, UR5 Universal Robotics, Standard DH-parameters: [theta, d, a, alpha], according to P. Corke, Links modeld as cylindrical tubes, Inertia from Parham M. Kebria2016 / Kuefeta2014


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`InverseKinematicsNumericalExample.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/InverseKinematicsNumericalExample.py) (Ex), [`ROSMobileManipulator.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/ROSMobileManipulator.py) (Ex), [`serialRobotInverseKinematics.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/serialRobotInverseKinematics.py) (Ex), [`systemContainerComputeOnlyTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/systemContainerComputeOnlyTest.py) (TM)


(sec-models-manipulatorpuma560)=
## Function: ManipulatorPuma560

[`ManipulatorPuma560()`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/models.py#L507)

- **function description**: generate puma560 manipulator as myRobot dictionary, settings are done in function
- **output**: myRobot dictionary
- **author**: Martin Sereinig
- **notes**: std DH-parameters: [theta, d, a, alpha], according to P. Corke page 138, the joint limits are those of the Robotics Toolbox 1.5 (160, -45..225, -225..45, -110..170, 100, 266 degrees); the inertias of links 0 and 2 are adjusted against Corke's data so that the principal moments fulfill the triangle inequality: link 0 has only I_yy = 0.35 there, the moment about its joint axis and the only one that acts, and gets I_xx = I_zz = 0.2; link 2 gets I_zz = 0.025 instead of 0.0125 (0.066 + 0.0125 < 0.086 is not physical)

(sec-models-manipulatorstaublitx2-90l)=
## Function: ManipulatorStaubliTX2_90L

[`ManipulatorStaubliTX2_90L()`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/models.py#L612)

- **function description**: generate the Staubli TX2-90L manipulator as robot dictionary, with the joint frames of its URDF (dhMode 'jointFrames': per link the joint type and the translation from the previous joint frame; all link frames parallel at q = 0, the arm upright); a 6R robot with a spherical wrist, for KinematicChain.InverseKinematicsAnalytic
- **output**: robot dictionary for LinkDict2Robot
- **notes**: the kinematics, the joint limits and the maximum joint velocities are those of tx2_90l.urdf of the ros-industrial staubli_experimental repository (https://github.com/ros-industrial/staubli_experimental, staubli_tx2_90_support); the URDF has no inertia data and the manufacturer gives only the total mass of 117 kg: the masses, centers of mass and inertias are those of the solids of the visual meshes with one density, 2032 kg/m^3, so that all links with the base (24.85 kg) have 117 kg, with 0.4 kg of link 5 given to link 6, whose motor and flange the meshes leave in link 5 (the densities of the two adjusted, #3371); estimates for simulation; the tool frame is the flange, 0.1 m after the wrist center; 'urdfGraphics' names the URDF file and its links for exudyn.robotics.urdfImport.AddURDFgraphics, which adds the meshes of the URDF


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`staubliTX2blending.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/staubliTX2blending.py) (Ex), [`staubliTX2trajectories.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/staubliTX2trajectories.py) (Ex), [`robotCartesianPathsTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotCartesianPathsTest.py) (TM), [`robotDictionaryTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotDictionaryTest.py) (TM), [`robotFrictionEndStopsTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotFrictionEndStopsTest.py) (TM), [`robotInverseDynamicsTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotInverseDynamicsTest.py) (TM), [`robotTrajectoryProfilesTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotTrajectoryProfilesTest.py) (TM), [`trajectoryBlendingCartesianTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/trajectoryBlendingCartesianTest.py) (TM), ...

(sec-models-linkdict2robot)=
## Function: LinkDict2Robot

[`LinkDict2Robot(robotLinkDict, robotClass = None, initialConfiguration = None, friction = False)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/models.py#L825)

- **function description**: generate serial manipulator as robotClass object from robotLinkDict
- **input**:
  - `robotClass`: robot class object from roboticsCore; if robotClass is provided, gravity, tool and base are used from there
  - `robotLinkDict`: list of robot links generated by manipulator import for individual robot dictionary
  - `initialConfiguration`: None: Robot.q0 is the reference configuration; 'model': the configuration the model names in 'initialConfiguration' (e.g. 'qr', the arm ready, as in the RTB); the name of one of the model's 'configurations' (e.g. 'qz', 'qr'); or the joint coordinates (#3277)
  - `friction`: if True, the 'viscousFriction' and 'coulombFriction' of the links of the model (where known, e.g. the Puma560) become those of the RobotLinks (#3277)
- **output**: updated robot class
- **author**: Martin Sereinig
- **notes**: dhMode 'stdDH', 'modDHKK' or 'jointFrames' (per link 'jointType' and 'preHT', the link frame the joint frame); the optional 'jointLimits' of a link become RobotLink jointLimits; 'configurations' are named joint coordinates of the model, as the configs of the Robotics Toolbox DH Parameter Information stdH = [theta, d, a, alpha] with Rz(theta) * Tz(d) * Tx(a) * Rx(alpha) modDH = [alpha, dx, theta, rz] with used by Corke and Lynch: Rx(alpha) * Tx(a) * Rz(theta) * Tz(d) used by Khali:           Rx(alpha) * Tx(d) * Rz(theta) * Tz(r) Important note:  d(khali)=a(corke)  and r(khali)=d(corke)


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`humanRobotInteraction.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/humanRobotInteraction.py) (Ex), [`InverseKinematicsNumericalExample.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/InverseKinematicsNumericalExample.py) (Ex), [`ROSMobileManipulator.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/ROSMobileManipulator.py) (Ex), [`serialRobotInteractiveLimits.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/serialRobotInteractiveLimits.py) (Ex), [`serialRobotInverseKinematics.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/serialRobotInverseKinematics.py) (Ex), [`analyticInverseKinematicsTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/analyticInverseKinematicsTest.py) (TM), [`kinematicChainTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/kinematicChainTest.py) (TM), [`numericalInverseKinematicsTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/numericalInverseKinematicsTest.py) (TM), ...
